newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU energy ministers served "solar coffee".
newsitem.headline: EU energy ministers served "solar coffee".

text.p: Greenpeace, urging the European Union to do more to cut emissions of carbon dioxide, served EU energy ministers coffee on Tuesday brewed, despite cold and rainy weather, in a mobile kitchen powered by the sun.

The environmentalist group was seeking a "strong commitment" from ministers to promote renewable energy sources such as wind, wood, wave and solar power to help reduce CO2 emissions, which can cause climate warming.
"The EU's commitment to renewable energy at present is completely inadequate," said Kirsty Hamilton, climate campaigner at Greenpeace.
Despite the unpromising weather, the solar cells provided some energy for the "solar kitchen", although back-up batteries -- charged by solar power on a sunnier day -- were also used.

EU Energy Commissioner Christos Papoutsis, Danish Energy Minister Svend Auken and Irish Energy Minister Emmet Stagg visited the kitchen before starting a ministerial debate on boosting the use of renewable energy in the EU.

The European Commission last month presented a strategy calling for the use of renewable energy sources to be doubled to 12 percent of total energy consumption by 2010, partly because of environmental reasons and to cut dependency on imported fuels.
But Greenpeace said the the proposal did not go anywhere near far enough, demanding a 20 percent cut of EU's CO2 emissions by 2005 to prevent "dangerous climate change."
